title: Consecutive-difference coordinates and invariant polynomial complex
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$. Put $A(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on the coherent profinite site [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ for $r\geq0$, with its product topology [def-sfb-ladic-lattice]. Use internal $A$-modules and internal $L$-actions [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module], in coefficient universes containing the site and every profinite parameter set [def-weil-size-convention].

For $n\geq0$, let $K^n$ be the internal direct sum of copies of $A$ on the monomials in the $(n+1)r$ variables $y_0,\ldots,y_n$, each an $r$-tuple [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Give it the diagonal action $(g\cdot f)(y_0,\ldots,y_n)=f(y_0-g,\ldots,y_n-g)$, for every section $g\in C(S,L)$, and the differential
$$(\delta f)(y_0,\ldots,y_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^if(y_0,\ldots,\widehat y_i,\ldots,y_{n+1}).$$
Set $K^n=0$ for $n<0$, and let $a:A[0]\to K$ include the constants, with trivial action on $A$.

Let $P^n$ be the internal polynomial direct sum on the $nr$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, each an $r$-tuple, zero in negative degrees, with differential
$$(dp)(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})=p(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^ip(x_1,\ldots,x_i+x_{i+1},\ldots,x_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}p(x_1,\ldots,x_n).$$

For each $n\geq0$ the substitutions $z=y_0$, $x_i=y_i-y_{i-1}$, with inverse $y_i=z+x_1+\cdots+x_i$, give an equivariant internal-module isomorphism from $K^n$ to the polynomial direct sum in $z,x_1,\ldots,x_n$, with $L$ translating only $z$ by $z\mapsto z-g$. Thus this is the translation module with $r$ translation variables and $nr$ fixed spectator variables. Its invariant submodule, where invariance is required after every profinite base change, consists exactly of the polynomials independent of $z$. More precisely, substitution of consecutive differences gives an isomorphism of cochain complexes
$$\phi:P^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}(K^\bullet)^L,\qquad (\phi^np)(y_0,\ldots,y_n)=p(y_1-y_0,\ldots,y_n-y_{n-1}).$$
Its inverse in degree $n$ is substitution of $(0,x_1,x_1+x_2,\ldots,x_1+\cdots+x_n)$. In particular $Q(\phi)$ is the specified isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The assertions concern sheaf direct sums, including their locally finite sections. They hold also for $n=0$ and $r=0$, for the latter giving the identity on each term $A$ of the unnormalized constant complex. No acyclicity of derived invariants is asserted here.

proof.text: For a finite variable set $V$, write $M_V=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^V}A$. Its finite partial sums have sections $A(S)^D$: finite products of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], and coordinatewise scalar action gives its module structure [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Coordinate inclusions and projections are linear and satisfy $\pi_a\iota_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $\sum_a\iota_a\pi_a=1$, so this is also the finite coproduct. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-action-filtered-colimit-creation] with the one-element compact profinite group and the filtered poset of finite subsets $D\subset\mathbf N^V$, assigning trivial actions to these partial sums. This poset is small in the stipulated universe. Its colimit is $M_V$: a compatible family of maps out of finite partial sums is exactly one map from each monomial summand. Consequently $M_V(S)=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^V}A(S)=A(S)[V]$ by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], naturally in $S$. For locally finite sections, refine to a finite covering in the coherent topology: the union of its finitely many monomial supports is finite. Thus the calculation includes sheaf direct-sum sections, not just a chosen degree bound.

proof.text: On the polynomial section rings of step 1, define $\Theta_n(f)=f(z,z+x_1,\ldots,z+x_1+\cdots+x_n)$. Polynomial evaluation in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] makes this an $A(S)$-linear map. Its inverse substitutes $z=y_0$, $x_i=y_i-y_{i-1}$: the prefix sums telescope to $y_i$, and subtracting adjacent prefix sums recovers $x_i$. Both identities hold on each variable and hence on every polynomial. These formulas commute with restriction of coefficients. For every $g\in C(S,L)$ they give $\Theta_n(g\cdot f)(z,x)=\Theta_n(f)(z-g,x)$, since every $y_i$ is decreased by the same $g$. Thus $\Theta_n$ is an equivariant internal-module isomorphism with $r$ translated and $nr$ spectator variables [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

proof.text: Let $q=\Theta_n(f)$ for an invariant section $f$ over $S$. By [def-sfb-condensed-action-module] it is fixed in particular by the constant lattice vectors $e_j$ [def-sfb-ladic-lattice]. Fix $j$ and regard $q$ as a polynomial in $z_j$ over $B=A(S)[z_k\ (k\ne j),x]$. If its degree in $z_j$ is $d>0$, with top coefficient $a_d\ne0$, the coefficient of $z_j^{d-1}$ in $q(z_j-1)-q(z_j)$ is $-d a_d$: the top term contributes $-d a_d$, the terms of degree $d-1$ cancel, and all smaller terms contribute zero. But $d$ is a unit of $A(S)=C(S,F)$, with inverse the continuous constant function $1/d$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. This contradicts translation invariance. Thus $q$ is independent of each $z_j$. The argument uses only a single finite polynomial at a time, as justified by step 1, and remains valid for rings with zero divisors; if $S$ is empty the section ring is zero.

proof.text: Conversely a polynomial $q=p(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ is fixed under $z\mapsto z-g$ for every section $g$, including after every $T\to S$: pullback changes only its coefficients and does not introduce $z$. This verifies the full parameterwise condition of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], not just invariance under constant lattice vectors. Step 3 and this converse identify the invariant submodule exactly with the spectator polynomial direct sum. In the original variables its inclusion is $\phi^n(p)=p(y_1-y_0,\ldots,y_n-y_{n-1})$. Evaluation at $(0,x_1,x_1+x_2,\ldots,x_1+\cdots+x_n)$ is its inverse: it sends the consecutive differences to $x_i$ and sends $f$ to $\Theta_n(f)(0,x)$, whose substitution back is $f$ by independence of $z$. All maps are internal $A$-linear and natural in the parameter set, by polynomial substitution [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

proof.text: The alternating deletion maps define a cochain differential on $K$. In $\delta^{n+1}\delta^n f$, the term deleting original coordinates $i<j$ occurs twice: deleting $i$ first then the coordinate originally at $j$ has sign $(-1)^{i+j-1}$, whereas deleting $j$ first then $i$ has sign $(-1)^{i+j}$. They cancel. Each deletion commutes with diagonal translation, so the differential restricts to the invariant submodules. The substitutions preserve constants; in degree zero $\delta^0(c)=c-c=0$, so the stated augmentation is an equivariant cochain map. All these identities are polynomial identities [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], hence internal identities by step 1.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-written homogeneous polynomial coordinate calculation below the delegated open-coefficient input.

proof.text: Compute the differential on $\phi^n(p)$. For a tuple $(y_0,\ldots,y_{n+1})$ set $x_i=y_i-y_{i-1}$. Deleting $y_0$ leaves differences $(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})$. Deleting an interior $y_i$, $1\le i\le n$, replaces the two adjacent differences by $y_{i+1}-y_{i-1}=x_i+x_{i+1}$ and leaves the others unchanged. Deleting $y_{n+1}$ leaves $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. Keeping the respective signs $1,(-1)^i,(-1)^{n+1}$ gives exactly $\delta^n\phi^n=\phi^{n+1}d^n$. These are equalities of polynomials [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], not just equalities of evaluated functions. Since each $\phi^n$ is an isomorphism and $\delta^2=0$, also $d^2=0$ and the degreewise inverses form a cochain map. Extend by the unique maps between zero modules in negative degrees to obtain the claimed cochain-complex isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent-written homogeneous polynomial coordinate calculation below the delegated open-coefficient input.

proof.text: For $n=0$ the spectator polynomial ring has no variables, so step 3 identifies $(K^0)^L$ with $A$, and $\phi^0$ is the constant inclusion with inverse evaluation at $0$. The two faces of $d^0$ cancel. For $r=0$ there are no variables and $L$ is the one-element group [def-sfb-ladic-lattice]; every coordinate substitution is the identity on $A$. In degree $n$, both differentials are multiplication by $\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i$ (zero for even $n$, the identity for odd $n$), so the unnormalized constant complexes, including their augmentations, agree. Finally the localization functor $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] sends $\phi$ and its explicit inverse to inverse morphisms, proving the specified derived isomorphism. No resolution or derived-invariant acyclicity enters this calculation.
